argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification for launch readiness in aggregate, but not a clean no-limitation certification. The strongest supportable position is that certification remains defensible if it is explicitly conditioned on correcting the model-card language to disclose that refund-policy summarization is a named deployment context with missing evaluation coverage. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passing general support, latency, and rollback checks support launch preparedness; they do not convert the named refund-policy summarization gap into a pass. On that record, the appropriate treatment is caveated compliance rather than escalation, provided the audit packet and model card state the gap as an unknown.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument changes the policy standard. The relevant governance point is narrower: escalation is unnecessary if the auditor treats this as a disclosure-conditioned certification issue rather than a clean-certification failure, because the admissible record already supports launch readiness in aggregate and identifies the precise caveat needed for policy alignment.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is clear that material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts must be disclosed. It also distinguishes general readiness evidence from named-context coverage. That means the current packet can support certification only if the certification is framed with the required disclosure; it cannot support a clean claim that there is no deployment limitation, and it cannot treat absence of failed completed tests as evidence that the named context passed.
concessions: The current draft model card language is not supportable as written because it says there are no known enterprise refund workflow limitations despite missing named-context eval coverage.
The record does not support any claim that refund-policy summarization is passed or effectively covered by general tests.
The record supports certification only in a caveated form that discloses the refund-policy summarization evaluation gap as an unknown.
